topics.name: Artificial Intelligence
topics.definition: Computer systems performing tasks that normally require human intelligence — perception, reasoning, language, decision-making.

topics.name: Machine Learning
topics.definition: Systems that improve at a task from data/experience rather than being explicitly programmed with rules for every case.

topics.name: Deep Learning
topics.definition: Machine learning using multi-layer neural networks to learn hierarchical representations directly from raw data.

topics.name: Neural Networks
topics.definition: Layered networks of simple weighted units (neurons) whose connection strengths are learned from data via backpropagation.

topics.name: Generative AI
topics.definition: Models that produce new content (text, code, images) rather than only classifying or scoring existing input.

topics.name: Foundation Models
topics.definition: Large models pre-trained on broad data, then adapted (via prompting or fine-tuning) to many downstream tasks — e.g. Claude.

topics.name: Transformer
topics.definition: The neural network architecture (attention-based, no recurrence) underlying modern large language models.

topics.name: Attention
topics.definition: The mechanism letting a model weigh how relevant each other token is when producing a representation for a given token.

topics.name: Token
topics.definition: The basic unit a language model reads/writes — a word, subword, or character fragment, not necessarily a whole word.

topics.name: Tokenization
topics.definition: Splitting raw text into tokens using a fixed vocabulary/algorithm before it can be fed to a model.

topics.name: Context Window
topics.definition: The maximum number of tokens (input + output) a model can attend to in a single call.

topics.name: Inference
topics.definition: Running a trained model forward to produce an output, as opposed to training/updating its weights.

topics.name: Sampling
topics.definition: The strategy for choosing the next token from the model's predicted probability distribution.

topics.name: Temperature
topics.definition: A sampling parameter controlling randomness — lower values make output more deterministic/focused.

topics.name: Top-p
topics.definition: Nucleus sampling — restricts token choice to the smallest set whose cumulative probability exceeds p.

topics.name: Hallucination
topics.definition: A model producing fluent but false or unsupported output — the core reason this project verifies claims against real tool results instead of trusting model output alone.

topics.name: System Prompt
topics.definition: Instructions given to a model before the conversation, establishing its role, constraints, and behavior.

topics.name: User Prompt
topics.definition: The end user's actual request/message to the model, as distinct from the system prompt.

topics.name: Prompt Engineering
topics.definition: Deliberately designing prompt wording/structure to reliably get the desired model behavior.

topics.name: Context Engineering
topics.definition: Deliberately curating WHAT information (files, retrieval results, tool schemas, history) is placed in the model's context, not just how it's worded.

topics.name: Structured Output
topics.definition: Constraining a model's response to a defined schema (e.g. a tool call) rather than free text.

topics.name: Few-shot Prompting
topics.definition: Including a few worked examples in the prompt to steer the model's output format/behavior.

topics.name: Context Management
topics.definition: Deciding what to keep, summarize, or drop as a conversation/session grows beyond what fits usefully in context.

topics.name: Embeddings
topics.definition: A numeric vector representation of text/code such that semantically similar content maps to nearby vectors.

topics.name: Semantic Search
topics.definition: Finding relevant content by embedding-vector similarity rather than exact keyword matching.

topics.name: Vector Database
topics.definition: A datastore specialized for storing and similarity-searching embedding vectors at scale.

topics.name: Similarity
topics.definition: A numeric measure (e.g. cosine similarity) of how close two embedding vectors are.

topics.name: Chunking
topics.definition: Splitting a document into smaller pieces before embedding, so retrieval can return precisely relevant sections.

topics.name: Metadata
topics.definition: Structured facts attached to a chunk/document (path, timestamps, type) used to filter or explain retrieval results.

topics.name: Hybrid Search
topics.definition: Combining semantic (vector) search with exact/keyword search or verification for better precision.

topics.name: Reranking
topics.definition: A second-pass model that reorders initial retrieval candidates by finer-grained relevance.

topics.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
topics.definition: Giving a model relevant retrieved content at inference time instead of relying only on what it memorized during training.

topics.name: Indexing
topics.definition: The offline step of chunking, embedding, and storing content so it can later be retrieved quickly.

topics.name: Retrieval
topics.definition: The online step of finding the most relevant stored chunks for a given query.

topics.name: Grounding
topics.definition: Tying a model's claims to real, checkable source content rather than unverified generation.

topics.name: Context Injection
topics.definition: Placing retrieved content directly into the prompt so the model can condition its answer on it.

topics.name: RAG Evaluation
topics.definition: Measuring whether retrieval actually returns relevant content and whether generation stays faithful to it.

topics.name: RAG Failure Modes
topics.definition: Ways RAG breaks in practice: irrelevant retrieval, stale index, over-trusting a retrieved-but-unverified chunk.

topics.name: Function Calling
topics.definition: A model's ability to emit a structured call to a predefined function/tool instead of only free text.

topics.name: Tool Calling
topics.definition: The general pattern of a model selecting and invoking external tools/actions as part of solving a task.

topics.name: Tool Schemas
topics.definition: The formal definition (name, description, input parameters) a model is given so it can call a tool correctly.

topics.name: Tool Authorization
topics.definition: The boundary deciding which tools a model may call and under what human/policy approval.

topics.name: Tool Result Handling
topics.definition: How a tool's real output is fed back to the model so it can continue reasoning from actual evidence, not a guess.

topics.name: MCP Architecture
topics.definition: Model Context Protocol's client-server design for exposing tools/data/prompts to any compliant AI client in a standard way.

topics.name: Clients
topics.definition: The MCP-side component (e.g. an AI application) that discovers and invokes a server's tools/resources.

topics.name: Servers
topics.definition: The MCP-side component exposing tools/resources/prompts over a standard protocol.

topics.name: Tools
topics.definition: MCP's concept for an invokable, schema-described action a server exposes to clients.

topics.name: Resources
topics.definition: MCP's concept for addressable, readable content a server exposes (distinct from an invokable tool).

topics.name: Prompts
topics.definition: MCP's concept for server-defined, reusable prompt templates a client can request.

topics.name: Transports
topics.definition: How MCP messages actually move between client/server — e.g. stdio (local process) or Streamable HTTP (networked).

topics.name: Authorization
topics.definition: MCP's mechanisms for controlling which client may access which server tools/resources.

topics.name: Current Protocol Concepts
topics.definition: The MCP spec version actually implemented against in this project, and what it changed (e.g. stateless Streamable HTTP).

topics.name: Agent Loop
topics.definition: The repeating cycle of a model reasoning, calling a tool, receiving a real result, and reasoning again until done.

topics.name: Planning
topics.definition: An agent deciding what steps to take before/while executing, rather than reacting one tool call at a time with no direction.

topics.name: Task Decomposition
topics.definition: Breaking a larger goal into smaller steps an agent (or set of agents) can execute and verify individually.

topics.name: State
topics.definition: What an agent tracks about progress/results across steps of a single run.

topics.name: Memory
topics.definition: What an agent/system persists across separate runs/sessions, distinct from in-run state.

topics.name: Tool Selection
topics.definition: An agent's decision of which available tool (if any) best serves the current step.

topics.name: Self-correction
topics.definition: An agent detecting its own tool/verification failure and adjusting its next step in response.

topics.name: Reflection
topics.definition: An agent explicitly reviewing its own prior output/reasoning before finalizing or continuing.

topics.name: Multi-agent Systems
topics.definition: Architectures where multiple distinct agents (often with different roles) collaborate on a task.

topics.name: Human-in-the-loop
topics.definition: A human must actively approve/decide before a consequential action proceeds — this project's core approval boundary.

topics.name: Human-on-the-loop
topics.definition: A human monitors and can intervene, but does not have to approve every individual action (used for this project's bounded-autonomy preview tier).

topics.name: Autonomy
topics.definition: The degree to which an agent may act without a human approving each step — deliberately scoped by risk in this project, never unconditional.

topics.name: Coding Agents
topics.definition: AI agents that read, propose, and (under authorization) modify real source code as part of their task.

topics.name: Repository Understanding
topics.definition: An agent building an accurate picture of an actual codebase's structure/conventions before proposing a change.

topics.name: Impact Analysis
topics.definition: Assessing what a proposed change actually touches/risks before applying it.

topics.name: Agentic SDLC
topics.definition: Extending the software delivery lifecycle (plan/build/test/deploy/verify) with AI agents performing bounded, verified steps.

topics.name: Verification Gates
topics.definition: Deterministic checks (compile, test, production HTTP check) a proposed change must pass before being considered successful — never taking a model's own claim as proof.

topics.name: Risk-based Autonomy
topics.definition: Granting more autonomous execution only for changes classified as small/low-risk/reversible; everything else requires explicit human authorization.

topics.name: Human Authority
topics.definition: The principle that capability (what an agent CAN technically do) never equals authority (what it's allowed to do without a human) — a named Constitution rule in this project.

topics.name: Production Verification
topics.definition: Independently checking the REAL deployed system after a change, rather than trusting a deploy tool's own status report.

topics.name: LLM Evaluation
topics.definition: Systematically measuring a model's output quality against defined criteria/data, not just spot-checking.

topics.name: Agent Evaluation
topics.definition: Evaluating an agent's full trajectory (tool choices, corrections, final outcome), not just one model response.

topics.name: Deterministic Tests
topics.definition: Tests with a fixed, repeatable pass/fail outcome — this project's primary correctness signal (unit tests, real compile/test runs).

topics.name: Regression Evals
topics.definition: Re-running past known-good/known-bad cases after a change to confirm nothing that used to work now breaks.

topics.name: Groundedness
topics.definition: Whether a model's claim is actually backed by real, checked evidence rather than asserted from unread/unverified content.

topics.name: Reliability
topics.definition: How consistently a system produces a correct/expected outcome across repeated real runs.

topics.name: First-pass Success
topics.definition: Whether an agent's first attempt at a task succeeds without requiring a human correction/retry.

topics.name: Failure Trajectories
topics.definition: The full sequence of steps/events leading to a failed outcome — deliberately preserved as evidence in this project's event ledger, not discarded.

topics.name: Prompt Injection
topics.definition: Malicious/untrusted content (in a file, tool result, or webpage) attempting to hijack a model's instructions.

topics.name: Tool Abuse
topics.definition: A model being tricked or misconfigured into using a legitimate tool for an unintended, harmful action.

topics.name: Least Privilege
topics.definition: Granting a model/agent only the exact tools/scope/paths it needs — never broad, unscoped access.

topics.name: Sandboxing
topics.definition: Isolating an agent's execution environment so a mistake or attack can't reach the real system unchecked.

topics.name: Secret Protection
topics.definition: Deterministically preventing credential-shaped values from ever reaching a model, log, or durable store.

topics.name: Data Classification
topics.definition: Explicitly tagging captured data (e.g. TRAINING_ALLOWED, EVAL_ONLY, SECRET_NEVER_STORE) so downstream use respects its real sensitivity.

topics.name: RAG Poisoning
topics.definition: An attacker planting malicious content where a retrieval system will find and surface it as if trustworthy.

topics.name: Approval Boundaries
topics.definition: The exact, verified line between what a model can propose and what only a human can authorize — enforced outside the model's own reachable tool surface in this project.

topics.name: AI Governance
topics.definition: The organizational rules/policies constraining how AI systems may act, what they may access, and who is accountable.

topics.name: AI Tracing
topics.definition: Recording the real sequence of a model/agent's calls and decisions so a run can be reconstructed after the fact.

topics.name: Events
topics.definition: Individual, timestamped, typed records of something that actually happened — this project's atomic unit of durable evidence.

topics.name: Spans
topics.definition: A tracing concept for a bounded operation with a start/end time, often nested (e.g. one tool call within one agent turn).

topics.name: Model Usage
topics.definition: Real, provider-reported facts about a model call (provider, model, token counts) — never estimated.

topics.name: Token Usage
topics.definition: The real input/output token counts a model call actually consumed, as reported by the API response itself.

topics.name: Latency
topics.definition: How long a real operation (model call, tool call, deployment) actually took, measured, not guessed.

topics.name: Human Wait Time
topics.definition: How long a human's attention/approval was genuinely needed before an agent could continue — captured as raw timestamps, never fabricated as a single number.

topics.name: Tool Telemetry
topics.definition: Structured records of real tool calls (name, input summary, success, duration) for later analysis.

topics.name: Agent Telemetry
topics.definition: Structured records of an agent's own development/runtime activity — this project's event ledger, distinguishing PRODUCT_DEVELOPMENT from PRODUCT_RUNTIME sources.

topics.name: Model Selection
topics.definition: Choosing which model to use for a given task based on capability/cost/latency tradeoffs.

topics.name: Model Routing
topics.definition: Automatically directing different requests to different models based on task type/complexity/cost.

topics.name: Fine-tuning
topics.definition: Further training a pre-trained model's weights on task-specific data to specialize its behavior.

topics.name: Preference Data
topics.definition: Human/AI-judged comparisons between candidate outputs, used to align a model toward preferred behavior.

topics.name: Evaluation Dataset
topics.definition: A held-out set of real or representative cases used to measure model/agent performance.

topics.name: Training Dataset
topics.definition: The data a model's weights are actually learned from.

topics.name: Distillation
topics.definition: Training a smaller model to imitate a larger one's behavior, trading some capability for cost/speed.

topics.name: Proprietary Models
topics.definition: Models trained/owned privately on an organization's own captured data — a stated future direction for this project's evidence ledger, not a current capability.

topics.name: Token Cost
topics.definition: The real monetary cost of a model call, derived from its real token counts and a dated provider pricing table.

topics.name: Latency
topics.definition: The real time cost of a model/tool call — a first-class economic factor alongside token cost.

topics.name: Cost per Verified Change
topics.definition: The real total cost (tokens + time) to produce one change that actually passed verification — this project's target unit economic metric, not yet computed.

topics.name: Human Minutes per Change
topics.definition: The real amount of human attention required to get one verified change through — distinct from AI wall-clock time.

topics.name: Model Efficiency
topics.definition: How much real verified value a model produces per token/dollar spent.

topics.name: Caching
topics.definition: Reusing a previous model/tool result instead of recomputing it, to save cost/latency.

sections.title: AI Delivery Engineering (concepts encountered while building this platform)

topics.name: Event Ledger
topics.definition: This project's real, append-only, durable store of observable engineering events (Workbench runtime + Claude Code development activity).

topics.name: Append-only Data
topics.definition: A storage pattern where records are only ever added, never modified/deleted in place — preserves history and failure evidence.

topics.name: Idempotency
topics.definition: An operation that can be safely retried without producing a duplicate/incorrect result — this project's event inserts are idempotent by event_id.

topics.name: Retry
topics.definition: Attempting a failed operation again, ideally combined with idempotency so a retry can never corrupt state.

topics.name: Durable Spool
topics.definition: A local fallback queue that holds events when a remote store is unreachable, synced later — never a substitute for the real durable store.

topics.name: PostgreSQL
topics.definition: The real relational database backing this project's event ledger (Railway-hosted).

topics.name: TCP Proxy
topics.definition: A public network endpoint forwarding to a database that otherwise only listens on a private network — how this project's laptop reaches its Railway Postgres instance.

topics.name: Private Networking
topics.definition: A cloud provider's internal-only network, unreachable from outside without an explicit public endpoint (e.g. a TCP proxy).

topics.name: SSE
topics.definition: Server-Sent Events — a one-way, HTTP-based streaming protocol this project uses for live run updates.

topics.name: Polling Fallback
topics.definition: Periodically re-fetching state as a safety net alongside a streaming transport, since this project proved SSE can silently drop a stream with zero error signal.

topics.name: State Machines
topics.definition: Modeling a run's lifecycle as a fixed set of states/transitions (e.g. PLANNING -> BUILDING -> DEPLOYED) so status is always well-defined.

topics.name: Deployment Verification
topics.definition: Confirming a deployment actually succeeded via independent evidence (a real HTTP check), never trusting a deploy tool's self-report alone.

topics.name: Git Evidence
topics.definition: Using real commit history/hashes as durable, checkable evidence of what code actually changed and when.

topics.name: CI/CD
topics.definition: Automated build/test/deploy pipelines triggered by code changes — not yet implemented in this project (deploys are still run manually).

topics.name: Production Observability
topics.definition: Real, live visibility into a deployed system's actual behavior/state, not just its build-time correctness.
